Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-3583", "title": "Dentures", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Dentures are false teeth made to replace teeth you have lost."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Complete dentures cover your entire upper or lower jaw."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Be careful when wearing dentures because they may make it harder for you to feel hot foods and liquids."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Also, you may not notice biting on a bone from your food."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "In the beginning, your dentist may want to see you often to make sure the dentures fit."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Over time, your mouth will change and you may need to have your dentures adjusted or replaced."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Be sure to let your dentist handle these adjustments."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If your dentures move too much in your mouth, denture adhesive may help."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "In some cases, your dentist may suggest that you switch to dental implants."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "They are permanent, and they replace both the roots and teeth."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Keep your dentures clean and free from food that can cause stains, bad breath, or swollen gums."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Brush them every day with a denture care product."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Take your dentures out of your mouth at night, and put them in water or a denture-cleansing liquid."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1382", "title": "Polymyalgia Rheumatica", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Polymyalgia rheumatica is a disorder that causes muscle pain and stiffness in your neck, shoulders, and hips."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is most common in women and almost always occurs in people over 50."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The main symptom is stiffness after resting."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Other symptoms include fever , weakness and weight loss."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "In some cases, polymyalgia rheumatica develops overnight."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The cause of polymyalgia rheumatica is unknown."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Your doctor will use your medical history, symptoms, and a physical exam to make the diagnosis."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Lab tests for inflammation may help confirm the diagnosis."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Polymyalgia rheumatica sometimes occurs along with giant cell arteritis , a condition that causes swelling of the arteries in your head."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Symptoms include headaches and blurred vision."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Doctors often prescribe prednisone, a steroid medicine, for both conditions."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "With treatment, polymyalgia rheumatica usually disappears in a day or two."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Without treatment, it usually goes away after a year or more."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-85", "title": "Parkinson's Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Parkinson's disease (PD) is a type of movement disorder ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It happens when nerve cells in the brain don't produce enough of a brain chemical called dopamine."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Sometimes it is genetic, but most cases do not seem to run in families."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Exposure to chemicals in the environment might play a role."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Symptoms begin gradually, often on one side of the body."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "They include: Trembling of hands, arms, legs, jaw and face Stiffness of the arms, legs and trunk Slowness of movement Poor balance and coordination As symptoms get worse, people with the disease may have trouble walking, talking, or doing simple tasks."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They may also have problems such as depression, sleep problems, or trouble chewing, swallowing, or speaking."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "There is no specific test for PD, so it can be difficult to diagnose."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Doctors use a medical history and a neurological examination to diagnose it."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "PD usually begins around age 60, but it can start earlier."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "A variety of medicines sometimes help symptoms dramatically."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Surgery and deep brain stimulation (DBS) can help severe cases."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "With DBS, electrodes are surgically implanted in the brain."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "They send electrical pulses to stimulate the parts of the brain that control movement."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-331", "title": "Oral Cancer", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Most oral cancers are squamous cell cancers ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They begin in the flat cells that cover the surfaces of your mouth, tongue, and lips."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The cancer cells may spread into deeper tissue as the cancer grows."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Most oral cancers are related to tobacco use, heavy alcohol use, or an HPV infection ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Who is more likely to develop oral cancer?"}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Anyone can get oral cancer, but you are more likely to develop it if you: Use tobacco or drink lots of alcohol."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Your risk of developing oral cancer is even higher if you do both."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Get frequent sun exposure (for lip cancer)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The symptoms of oral cancer may include: A white or red patch in your mouth A lip or mouth sore that won't heal Bleeding, pain, or numbness in the lip or mouth Loose teeth or dentures that no longer fit well Problems or pain with swallowing A lump in your neck Ear pain Trouble moving your mouth or jaw Swelling of the jaw A sore throat or feeling that something is caught in the throat If you have any of these symptoms for more than two weeks, see your health care provider or dentist."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Oral cancer can spread quickly, so it's important to find it early."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "To find out if you have oral cancer, your provider may use: A physical exam of the lips and mouth."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "A biopsy or other procedure to collect cells from the lip or oral cavity."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The cells are viewed under a microscope to find out if they are abnormal."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "What are the treatments for oral cancer?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The treatments for oral cancer include surgery, radiation therapy , or both."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "After surgery, some people also need chemotherapy to kill any cancer cells that are left."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "There are steps you can take to help prevent oral cancer: Not smoking Limiting alcohol use or not drinking at all Getting regular dental exams NIH: National Cancer Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1327", "title": "Foot Health", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Each step you take involves a complex network of bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This, combined with all of the weight they carry, explains why feet can have problems."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "To keep your feet healthy: Examine your feet regularly Wear comfortable shoes that fit Wash your feet daily with soap and lukewarm water Trim your toenails straight across and not too short Your foot health can be a clue to your overall health."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "For example, joint stiffness could mean arthritis."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Tingling or numbness could be a sign of diabetes."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Swelling might indicate kidney disease, heart disease, or high blood pressure."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Good foot care and regular foot checks are an important part of your health care."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If you have foot problems, be sure to talk to your doctor."}]}]
